Markdown: body: "
About
BucketValue
A modelled stat line for every NBA player in every game, built the same way as its siblings DiamondValue (MLB) and GridironValue (NFL): models trained on the 2018-19 to 2025-26 seasons, with box-score history back to 2014-15, validated season by season on games they never saw, and shown as the median outcome for a player who plays.
"

Markdown: body: "
Where the numbers come from. Box scores, schedules, rosters and participation from NBA.com. Game lines from ESPN (DraftKings). Availability from the NBA's official injury report, read as of the time a projection is made, not as of tip-off.
What they are not. A forecast of what will happen, or betting advice. The posted line already prices most of what any model knows, so a gap between the two is information to weigh, not an edge to bet.
How to read a game page. MIN is the projected average for a player who plays. Every other column is a median if he plays: half of his outcomes land above it and half below. FS is the exception: PrizePicks' Fantasy Score formula (PTS + 1.2 REB + 1.5 AST + 3 STL + 3 BLK - TOV) on the numbers shown in its row, which is also the number a Fantasy Score line is judged against. P(play), the chance he plays at all, appears only for a player on the injury report or below 90%. Projections freeze 5 minutes before tip-off and never change after that. A provisional projection (made for a later date, or before the latest box scores were in) is shown as published but is never frozen.
How it is built. Three kinds of gradient-boosted model per player and game: the chance he plays at all, his minutes if he plays, and a per-minute rate for each stat, so a stat's projection is minutes times rate. Each is trained only on what was known before the game: earlier box scores, the game's spread and total, and the injury report as filed at the time. Each team's projected minutes are then pulled part of the way toward the 241.5 an average game holds (240 plus overtime), moving bench minutes more than starters' and never a player listed Out. Last, every player's game is simulated 3,000 times, with minutes errors measured by role and shots drawn so the points always add up, and the medians shown come from those simulations, centred on the model's own numbers.
What version 1 does not do. It projects regular-season games only: no preseason, play-in, playoff or NBA Cup final. Nothing changes after the freeze, so a scratch announced after the last injury report is not in the numbers until you mark him out on the game page. The board does not price period lines (halves, quarters, first minutes), Dunks, double-doubles or two-player squares, and the model does not price PrizePicks' Reboot rule (a More pick voided when a player leaves in the first half and does not return).
"

Markdown: body: "
Each edge is the worst of the 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 seasons, every one of them out of sample: percentage points of sides called correctly above always taking the more common side.
The lines were PROXY half-point lines built from a baseline projection, not real PrizePicks lines. A posted line already prices most of what a model knows, so against a real board expect less than these edges.
A combination line (Pts+Rebs+Asts, Blks+Stls, Fantasy Score and the rest) inherits the tier of its weakest component, so the board never trusts a combo more than its least reliable part. Its own measurement is shown beside it.
The tier is the order the board ranks rows in: a strong stat's lean outranks a weak stat's, whatever the size of either gap.
Biggest discrepancies, under the board, sorts the same shown lines by the size of the gap instead: standard lines only, in each stat's own units, with a stat-family filter for comparing like with like. It is a display, not a ranking of picks: a large gap is as often the model's miss as the line's.
"

Markdown: body: "
What it takes to break even. A two-pick Power Play pays 3 times the entry, so the pair has to hit at least one time in three: each pick needs about 57.7% just to break even. Across PrizePicks play sizes the per-pick break-even runs from 54.7% to 58.5%. An edge of a few points over the more common side is a long way from that.
The board is at its ceiling. A posted line is set by people who see the same box scores, injury reports and lines the models see, and it moves with the money. It already prices most of what a model knows, so the comparison on this site shows where the model disagrees with the line, not an edge over it. Read a large gap as a question to look into.
